title: Subsets II
keyIdea: Sort, then backtrack: each call saves current first, then for i from index: skip a value equal to the previous one at the same level (i > index && nums[i] == nums[i − 1]); push, recurse with i + 1, pop.

approaches.name: All subsets, then a set
approaches.idea: Sort, generate all 2ⁿ subsets with a bitmask, keep them in a set.
approaches.why: Builds every repeated subset and pays for the set.

approaches.name: Sorted backtracking, skip duplicates
approaches.idea: Save current; for i from index: skip equal-at-this-level; push, dfs(i + 1), pop.
approaches.why: Each distinct subset is generated exactly once.

quiz.q: Why save current at the start of each call?
options: Every call's current subset is a new answer, including the empty one
It must be at the end

quiz.q: Why is the skip condition i > index and not i > 0?
options: The first copy at each level is allowed; only further copies at the same level repeat subsets
So equal values are adjacent and the skip check works
